nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The local developer exploring the recovered model in the es-view SPA. Here they right-click stickies, overview boxes, sidebar items, and hotspot cards to gather them into a context bundle, then review, prune, or clear the set before handing it to Claude.

nodes.label: AddContextItem
nodes.description: Add one typed reference { type: node | flow | hotspot, id } to the curated context bundle. Idempotent: re-adding an already-present item is a silent no-op that preserves insertion order.

tactical.explanation: Triggered by the right-click 'Add ... to context bundle' menu item (ContextMenu.jsx) or, for removal's inverse, the same toggle. The React store's addToContext(type, id) calls api.js addContext -> POST /api/context { type, id }. The server route delegates to the addContextItem command (application/commands/add-context-item.ts), which validates the ref via itemExists (see inv-bundle-item-exists) and, on success, calls bundle.add(type, id), which inserts into the in-memory Map keyed by `type:id` only when the key is absent. The response returns the whole ordered bundle, which the store writes to bundleItems so the pill count and drawer re-render.

anchors.note: POST /api/context branch: calls addContextItem(services, bundle, type, id)
guard via itemExists then bundle.add(type, id)
Map.set only when key absent (dedup, insertion-ordered)

nodes.label: RemoveContextItem
nodes.description: Remove one typed reference from the context bundle. Idempotent and unguarded: removing an item that is not present succeeds as a no-op, and unlike add it does NOT check that the id exists in the model.

tactical.explanation: Triggered two ways: the right-click 'Remove ... from context bundle' toggle (ContextMenu.jsx) or the per-row ✕ in the drawer (ContextBundle.jsx). Both call the store's removeFromContext(type, id) -> api.js removeContext -> DELETE /api/context { type, id }. The DELETE branch does NOT run itemExists; it calls the removeContextItem command (application/commands/remove-context-item.ts), which calls bundle.remove(type, id), a plain Map.delete on `type:id` (no-op if absent). Returns the updated ordered bundle.

anchors.note: DELETE with id -> removeContextItem (no existence guard)

nodes.label: ClearContextBundle
nodes.description: Empty the entire context bundle in one action. Distinguished from RemoveContextItem by the absence of an id in the DELETE body.

tactical.explanation: Triggered by the drawer's 'Clear' button (ContextBundle.jsx) -> store clearBundle() -> api.js clearContext -> DELETE /api/context with NO body. The server DELETE branch: when body.id is falsy it falls through to the clearContextBundle command (application/commands/clear-context-bundle.ts) -> bundle.clear() (Map.clear) and returns { items: [] }. The store then sets bundleItems to []. So add/remove/clear all share the DELETE verb but branch on presence of an id.

anchors.note: DELETE with no id -> clearContextBundle -> { items: [] }

nodes.label: Context Bundle
nodes.description: The curated set of items the operator has gathered for Claude: an insertion-ordered collection of typed refs { type: node | flow | hotspot, id }, deduped by `type:id`. Lives purely in the shared in-memory server state (never persisted); the same Map is read by the SPA drawer AND by connected Claude/MCP sessions. Its consistency boundary is the add-time existence guard.

tactical.explanation: Implemented by the ContextBundle class (domain/session/context-bundle.ts) as `private readonly bundle = new Map()` keyed `${type}:${id}` -> { type, id, at }. add() inserts only when the key is absent (dedup + preserves order); remove() deletes by key; clear() empties it; list() projects to [{ type, id }] in insertion order. The aggregate's only enforced rule (a valid model ref) is applied by the addContextItem command before bundle.add, not inside the ContextBundle class itself. Rendering to markdown (application/read-models/context.ts renderBundleMarkdown) is a read-side projection, not aggregate state.

anchors.note: bundle = new Map(); the aggregate's state

fields.name: items
fields.derivation: The ordered list of gathered refs, one per gathered node/flow/hotspot, each { type, id }. Backed by a Map keyed `type:id`, so at most one entry per (type,id); iteration order is insertion order. Held only in process memory (a stored `at` timestamp per entry is dropped by getBundle and not exposed).

nodes.label: A bundle item must reference a real model node/flow/hotspot of its type
nodes.description: ERROR-level guard on AddContextItem: the POST /api/context route rejects (404) any add whose { type, id } does not resolve to an existing node, flow, or hotspot of that type, so the bundle can never hold a dangling ref. NOTE the guard is asymmetric: it runs only on add (POST); RemoveContextItem (DELETE) is unguarded but idempotent, so no stale ref can survive.

tactical.explanation: In the addContextItem command (application/commands/add-context-item.ts), `if (!id || !itemExists(services, type, id)) return { ok: false, error: ... }` runs before bundle.add, and the server route maps a not-ok result to HTTP 404. itemExists (application/read-models/items.ts) dispatches by type: flow -> model.flows.some(id); hotspot -> indexes.hotspotById.has(id); else -> indexes.nodeById.has(id). The same guard backs POST /api/comments and GET /api/item. The dedup rule (no duplicate `type:id`) is enforced inside ContextBundle.add itself but is a silent no-op, not a rejection, so it is folded here rather than modeled as a second invariant.

anchors.note: guard: not-found when !itemExists, mapped to HTTP 404 by the route
type-dispatched existence check against the model/indexes

nodes.label: ContextItemAdded
nodes.description: A node, flow, or hotspot has been gathered into the context bundle. The fact holds only for a genuinely new ref; re-adding an existing item is absorbed silently and raises nothing.

tactical.explanation: Realized by ContextBundle.add inserting a new `type:id` entry into the Map and returning the updated ordered bundle. Observable to the operator as the pill count incrementing and a new drawer row, and to a connected Claude session as an extra item in the event-storming://selected-nodes resource on its next read.

nodes.label: ContextItemRemoved
nodes.description: A single item has been dropped from the context bundle (via the right-click toggle or the drawer ✕). Idempotent: a remove of an absent item still returns the (unchanged) bundle.

tactical.explanation: Realized by ContextBundle.remove deleting the `type:id` key and returning the updated ordered bundle. Surfaced by the store overwriting bundleItems, shrinking the drawer list and pill count.

nodes.label: ContextBundleCleared
nodes.description: The entire context bundle has been emptied in one action, resetting it to the boot state.

tactical.explanation: Realized by ContextBundle.clear() calling Map.clear(); the server returns { items: [] } and the store sets bundleItems to []. Modeled as a distinct event from ContextItemRemoved because it is a separate command (bulk reset, no id) with its own DELETE branch.

nodes.label: Context bundle drawer & pill
nodes.description: What the operator reads to review the gathered set: the slide-over drawer listing each item as a colored row (label, type, ✕) plus the count on the Context pill. Backed by the bundleItems array the store keeps in sync from every add/remove/clear response. GET /api/context also returns a rendered markdown projection of the same set, which the 'Copy all for Claude' clipboard export and the MCP resource reuse (both modeled by other flows).

tactical.explanation: The store loads the bundle once on mount (getContext -> setBundleItems) and thereafter overwrites bundleItems from each mutation response, so the drawer/pill reflect server truth without re-fetching. ContextBundle.jsx maps bundleItems to rows via meta(item), resolving each ref's label/color from nodeById / hotspotById / model.flows. GET /api/context on the server calls the listContextBundle query (application/queries/list-context-bundle.ts), which returns { items, markdown } where markdown = renderBundleMarkdown(services, items) (application/read-models/context.ts) — that markdown is the read-side projection the copy-for-claude flow and the event-storming://selected-nodes MCP resource render; this flow only writes the underlying set.

anchors.note: markdown projection reused by copy/MCP flows

nodes.label: Connected Claude (MCP client)
nodes.description: A Claude session connected to the es-view MCP endpoint over streamable HTTP. It reads the bundle the operator built by @-mentioning the event-storming://selected-nodes resource, which returns the same in-memory set rendered as grounded markdown. The MCP read itself is a separate flow; this flow only references it as the downstream consumer.

tactical.explanation: mcp-server.ts registers the resource 'selected-nodes' at event-storming://selected-nodes; its read handler returns renderBundleMarkdown(services, bundle.list()) over the SAME shared ContextBundle instance the /api/context routes mutate, so a browser add is visible to Claude on its next resource read.

nodes.label: In-process session state
nodes.description: The single in-memory Selection and ContextBundle instances created at server boot in the CLI composition root, holding the current selection and the context-bundle Map. Non-persistent (lost on restart, never written to disk) and process-global: one pair of instances is shared by all browser tabs and all MCP sessions in the run. The bundle instance is what this flow writes.

tactical.explanation: adapters/cli/es-view.ts's runView constructs `new Selection()` and `new ContextBundle()` once and passes both instances to startServer/createServer (HTTP route handlers) and createMcpHandler (every MCP session), which is why a click in the SPA is what a connected Claude reads.

anchors.note: single shared Selection + ContextBundle instances constructed once

flows.name: Operator builds a context bundle for Claude
flows.summary: In the es-view SPA the operator right-clicks any sticky, overview box, sidebar item, glossary chip, or hotspot card and picks 'Add to context bundle' to gather it; the same menu (or the drawer ✕) removes an item, and the drawer's 'Clear' empties the set. Each action posts to /api/context, which validates that an added ref resolves to a real model node/flow/hotspot before mutating the shared in-memory bundle Map, then returns the whole ordered set the drawer and Context-pill count re-render from. The bundle lives only in process memory and is shared with connected Claude sessions, which later read it as the event-storming://selected-nodes MCP resource (a separate flow). The point is to let a human hand-curate exactly the grounded slice of the model Claude should reason over.
flows.trigger: Right-click any node/flow/hotspot in the SPA -> 'Add to context bundle' (ContextMenu.jsx:46); remove via the same toggle or the drawer ✕; clear via the drawer's 'Clear' button.

hotspots.label: One process-global bundle is shared by every browser tab and every Claude session
hotspots.description: The context bundle is a single in-memory Map on the one shared state object, with no per-client or per-session scoping. If two browser tabs (or two people on the same es-view URL) are open, or one operator curates while a Claude session reads, they all mutate and see the SAME bundle: an add in one tab appears in the other, and a 'Clear' wipes everyone's set. For the intended single-local-developer workflow this is the feature (the SPA click is exactly what Claude reads). Human question: is single-user, single-run the only supported mode, or should the bundle be scoped per browser session / per MCP session once es-view is ever shared or multi-tab? Restart also silently drops the bundle (no persistence).

tactical.explanation: runView constructs one `ContextBundle` instance (adapters/cli/es-view.ts:60); the server passes that same instance to all HTTP handlers and every MCP session, and list/add/remove/clear all operate on it with no client identity. The MCP resource reads the identical instance (mcp-server.ts:92). There is no keying by tab, cookie, or Mcp-Session-Id.

anchors.note: single global bundle Map, no per-client scope
all /api/context calls mutate the one shared bundle instance
MCP resource reads the same bundle.list()
